title: Tola, Jair, and Israel's Renewed Oppression

date.label: Undated Judges narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Tola and Jair are each given tenure figures but no narrated military exploit
claims.evidence: Judges 10:1–5 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

claims.claim: Judges 10 attributes oppression to both Philistines and Ammonites
claims.evidence: Judges 10:7–9 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the text alone does not externally corroborate the narrated events.

claims.claim: Judges 10:4 reports thirty towns belonging to Jair's thirty sons, called Havvoth-jair, in Gilead; the source does not identify thirty excavated sites.
claims.evidence: Judges 10:4 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). The text reports thirty towns belonging to Jair's thirty sons, called Havvoth-jair, in Gilead; the source does not identify thirty excavated sites. Tyson (Oxford Bibliographies, Introduction extract read in full) records the Ammonite core-territory geography and the ninth-century earliest evidence naming the Ammonites; the full annotated bibliography was not accessible. No exact historical identification, event proof, dates or mapped coordinates are asserted.
